oil.summary: A sharply bifurcated session for crude today. WTI surged +3.99% to $103.44/bbl, extending its one-month gain to over 9%, while Brent slipped -1.33% to $111.66 — still within striking distance of the $120 level flagged in today's commentary. The divergence likely reflects basis moves and physical market softness: Middle East physical crude reportedly eased even as paper benchmarks remain elevated. The macro backdrop is unambiguously bullish: the US-Iran conflict continues to threaten Strait of Hormuz flows, Iran has explicitly targeted Saudi refineries, and Egypt is now drawn into the Saudi defense posture. Non-Iran regional exports have recovered via Hormuz alternatives, capping the upside somewhat. Distillates sold off hard — heating oil -2.60%, RBOB -1.54% — suggesting demand concerns or profit-taking after a volatile week. A CFTC probe into a 6-million-barrel two-minute futures dump adds a market-integrity dimension to watch. Venezuela supply increments (~20,000 bbl/day) and the first Russian diesel cargo bound for New York offer marginal offsets to tightness.
drivers: US-Iran war and explicit Iranian threats to Saudi refining infrastructure keep geopolitical risk premium elevated, pushing Brent near five-month highs
Middle East physical crude softening and partial Hormuz alternative routing limit upside, contributing to WTI/Brent divergence
Distillate weakness (HO -2.60%, RBOB -1.54%) and CFTC scrutiny of a 6-million-barrel flash-sell event introduce near-term downside risks to refined products

gas.summary: Natural gas saw a strong single-day bounce on both sides of the Atlantic, though the weekly and monthly pictures diverge sharply by region. Henry Hub jumped +8.99% on the day to $3.047/MMBtu, but remains down -2.21% on the week and -7.58% on the month, suggesting today's move may be short-covering rather than a fundamental re-rating. TTF, by contrast, is up +3.62% today and has surged +24.22% over the past month to €93.3/MWh, reflecting European supply anxiety that dwarfs the US picture. Headline news flow specific to gas is thin today: Oil India announced a gas discovery in the shallow Krishna-Godavari Basin, and the US rig count held flat for a second consecutive week despite surging oil prices — indicating producers remain disciplined on gas-directed drilling.
drivers: Henry Hub single-day spike of nearly +9% likely driven by short-covering; monthly trend remains negative, suggesting no fundamental demand shift yet
TTF +24% over the past month points to sustained European supply tightness, amplified by Middle East conflict spillovers affecting LNG routing
Flat US rig count for second consecutive week signals producers are not chasing higher oil prices with incremental gas-directed drilling

power.summary: Power and carbon market-specific news flow is limited today. EU carbon (EUA) edged up +0.93% to $82.26/EUA, holding a narrow positive trend across all time horizons — weekly +0.38%, monthly +0.65% — suggesting a stable but unexciting carbon price environment. The most relevant driver for European power costs is TTF natural gas, up +3.62% on the day and +24.22% over the past month, which mechanically pressures gas-fired power generation margins and supports EUA prices at the margin. The broader geopolitical backdrop — Iranian threats to Gulf energy infrastructure, ongoing US-Iran conflict — sustains fossil fuel cost uncertainty that indirectly supports carbon pricing. A NASA-developed freeze-resistant battery was noted in feeds as a potential long-run EV technology, but has no near-term market relevance.
drivers: TTF at €93.3/MWh (+24% month-on-month) is the primary upward cost driver for European gas-fired power generation, supporting carbon pass-through pricing
EUA at $82.26 (+0.93% today) continues its low-volatility drift higher; Middle East supply risk sustains a modest geopolitical bid
Headline flow specific to power and carbon is sparse today; NASA battery story has no near-term market impact
